jurisdiction: North Carolina (Duke Energy Carolinas and Duke Energy Progress)
title: Duke large-load tariff settlement sets 50 MW / 80% or 150 MW applicability and 75% minimum billing on Schedule HLF

facts.dockets: E-7 Sub 1329 (Duke Energy Carolinas) and E-2 Sub 1380 (Duke Energy Progress)
facts.applicability: (a) total contract demand of 50 MW or more with expected 12-month rolling average load factor of 80% or more, or (b) total contract demand of 150 MW or more and any load factor; incremental service meeting the criteria and added on or after June 1, 2026 is subject to the provisions
facts.minimum_billing_demand: 75% of contract demand for all demand charges
facts.next_milestone: NCUC order on the settlement; no decision date announced as of 2026-10-18 per the existing record

summary: A Duke large-load tariff settlement filed in E-7 Sub 1329 and E-2 Sub 1380 would move covered data-center-scale customers to Schedule HLF, with billing demand floored at 75% of contract demand. Coverage applies at 50 MW and 80% load factor, or 150 MW at any load factor. The NCUC has not ruled.
source_title: SELC — Duke Energy large load tariff settlement (filed Oct. 6, 2026)
verbatims: a total contract demand of 50 MW or more and an expected 12-month rolling average load factor of 80% of more
will not be less than 75% of contract demand for all demand charges
The customer will be served under Schedule HLF

title: Florida SB 484 directs the PSC to require large-load tariffs so data centers pay their own cost of service

facts.governor_action: signed by Gov. Ron DeSantis on Thursday, May 7, 2026 (WFSU report published May 8)
facts.required: PSC to implement large load customer tariff and service requirements for public electric utilities
facts.cost_rule: tariff must reasonably ensure large load customers pay their own cost of service; nonpayment risk may not be borne by the general body of ratepayers
facts.local_control: preserves local government comprehensive-planning and land-development authority over large load customers
facts.unverified_secondary_details: 50 MW large-load threshold; utility tariff filings due Oct 1 2026; effective July 1 2026; OPPAGA study due July 1 2027; chapter number 2026-65. These come from secondary coverage and are not verified against the bill text.

summary: Florida enacted SB 484 in May 2026. It requires the PSC to implement large-load tariffs for investor-owned and public electric utilities that make data centers pay their own cost of service, and it preserves local land-use authority.
source_title: Florida Senate — Bill Summary, CS/CS/SB 484 (Data Centers); WFSU — Gov. DeSantis has signed a bill regulating data centers in Florida
verbatims: Requires the Public Service Commission (PSC) to implement large load customer tariff and service requirements for public electric utilities.

The tariff requirements must reasonably ensure that large load customers (such as large data centers) pay for their own cost of service, the risk of nonpayment of such costs may not be borne by the general body of ratepayers
Florida utility customers won't bear the additional costs brought by new large scale data centers that power artificial intelligence, under a bill signed by Gov. Ron DeSantis on Thursday.
notes: PRE-WINDOW: signed May 7, before the 2026-08-01 window. Included because it is not in the records and falls within the unit's state-bill scope; drop it if the window is strict.
